faultsAddressed.was: spawn stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] closed the inherited exclusive fd 9; the child preflight requires --heavy-lock-fd 9
faultsAddressed.fix: validateInheritedLockFd() proves the handed descriptor is open and points at the lock file (the wrapper never opens or flocks anything); buildStdio() keeps 0/1/2, fills 3..8 with 'ignore' and places the PARENT's descriptor at CHILD fd 9; the child argv now carries --heavy-lock <path> --heavy-lock-fd 9, the same number.
faultsAddressed.proof: C16 spawns a REAL cpu-only node grandchild under a real 'exec 9>LOCK; flock -x 9' through the wrapper's OWN buildStdio: the grandchild reports readlink(/proc/self/fd/9)==lock, fstat(9) dev+inode identical to the lock file, and an independent 'flock -n -x' FAILS (the inherited flock is real). The grandchild never takes a second lock: the contention probe is non-blocking and immediate. C16b covers missing/low/wrong-target/unopened fd refusals.

faultsAddressed.was: verifySinkOwnership called with sinkIndex:null while real sink-input rows carry the NUMERIC sink index, so a real stream could never match
faultsAddressed.fix: resolveSinkIndex() parses `pactl list short sinks` and returns the EXACT numeric index of the newly created sink; missing, ambiguous (duplicate name) and non-numeric index all REFUSE. verifySinkOwnership now refuses outright on an unresolved index instead of silently matching a name.
faultsAddressed.proof: C17 drives the ACTUAL wrapper functions with realistic multi-row pactl fixtures (alsa hdmi + null sink) and a realistic 'Sink: 2' sink-input row; C17a runs the ACTUAL runCombinedCapture end to end against those fixtures. PID-tree ownership refusal retained and re-asserted (foreign pid on the owned numeric index => foreign-stream-on-owned-sink).

faultsAddressed.was: the probe child was scoped inside try and never stopped or waited on pid/ownership/timeout failure; the finally stopped only the recorder and the sink
faultsAddressed.fix: the child handle is declared before the try and owned from the instant spawn returns. stopProbe() runs in the finally on EVERY path: it writes a bounded cooperative stop-request.json, sends SIGTERM to ITS OWN child only, waits up to 25 s for real exit, escalates to SIGKILL with an 8 s bound, then reads the probe's cleanup-receipt.json. The sink module is unloaded only AFTER that, and the wrapper exits (which is when root's heavy lock is released) only after it. The probe gained a bounded stop path: SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP and the stop file both route through the SAME createOwnedSessionGuard stopOnce(), closing the probe's OWN adopted browser and writing a receipt; a 20 s unref'd hard-exit timer bounds it. Errors during bring-up and the sampler still clean up through the pre-existing adopt-first path.
faultsAddressed.proof: C17a (ownership refusal), C17b (child 'error' event + no pid), C17c (session timeout) each inject a real failure into the ACTUAL runCombinedCapture and assert: stop file written, SIGTERM sent, no live child after the finally, teardown receipt observed, teardown order recorder -> probe -> sink unload. C17e greps both files for pkill/killall/pgrep/global chrome/34413 and finds none: only the wrapper's own child handle is ever signalled.

faultsAddressed.was: the session deadline began AFTER up to 120 s pid wait + 90 s ownership wait, so the claimed 360 s whole bound was really 570 s; child 'error' events were unhandled
faultsAddressed.fix: ONE absolute deadline is taken at session start and every wait (pid, ownership, probe, recheck) is bounded by remaining(). 'error' handlers on both the child and the recorder record spawnErrors and abort instead of hanging. The recorder is stopped and reaped, then the exact module is unloaded, on every path.
faultsAddressed.proof: C17c: a 4 s maxSessionS run finishes in seconds, the record proves sessionDeadlineMs - sessionStartMs == 4000, the failure is the absolute-bound path, and the recorder/sink/child are all torn down.
